findings.title: Mutable default `timezone.now()` evaluated once at class definition time
findings.body: The `queued` field uses `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` as a dataclass default. Unlike `field(default_factory=...)`, this calls `timezone.now()` exactly once when the module is imported, so every `AssignmentSource` created without an explicit `queued` value (which is every call site, including `from_integration`) gets the same stale timestamp — the process start time. The field is named `queued` and clearly intended to record when the assignment was queued, but it will report a time that can be arbitrarily far in the past (e.g., days for a long-running worker), making it useless for debugging sync loops or ordering, and misleading in logs/analytics. It should be `queued: datetime = field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

findings.title: `from_dict` silently swallows deserialization errors and returns None, defeating the cycle-break
findings.body: `AssignmentSource.from_dict` wraps `cls(**input_dict)` in `try/except (ValueError, TypeError): return None`. The dict is produced by `to_dict()` (via `asdict`), which serializes `queued` as a `datetime` object. When this dict is passed through the Celery task queue (`sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(kwargs={... "assignment_source_dict": assignment_source.to_dict() ...})` in `src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py:141`), the datetime is JSON-serialized to a string. On the worker side, `from_dict` then calls `AssignmentSource(source_name=..., integration_id=..., queued="2024-...Z")` — the dataclass performs no type coercion, so `queued` becomes a `str` rather than raising. Worse, if the payload contains any unexpected/missing key (e.g., a `TypeError` from a missing required argument, or a `ValueError`), `from_dict` returns `None`, and in `sync_assignee_outbound.py:56` a `None` source means `should_sync("outbound_assignee", None)` passes the cycle check — the exact loop this PR is meant to prevent silently reappears. The round-trip through the task queue is not actually tested (the new tests only cover `from_dict` with plain dicts, never a serialized-then-deserialized datetime), so this failure mode is invisible. `from_dict` should either coerce `queued` (e.g., `datetime.fromisoformat` / `django.utils.dateparse.parse_datetime`) or fail loudly rather than returning `None`.

findings.title: Cycle prevention compares `integration_id` against `org_integration.integration_id`, but the source is built from the Integration model id — mismatched id spaces
findings.body: In `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync`, the guard is `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id`. `AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration)` (called in `src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py:98,115` with the `RpcIntegration`) sets `integration_id=integration.id` — the id of the `Integration` model row. `self.org_integration` is an `OrganizationIntegration` row, and `OrganizationIntegration.integration_id` is the FK to `Integration`, so `self.org_integration.integration_id` is also the `Integration` id. So the comparison is actually consistent — but this is subtle and fragile: the field is named `integration_id` on a source that could plausibly be constructed from an `OrganizationIntegration` (whose own `.id` is a different id space), and nothing in the dataclass or its tests pins down which id is meant. If any future caller passes an `OrganizationIntegration` (or its id) the guard silently never matches and the sync loop returns. At minimum this deserves a test that exercises the real `sync_group_assignee_inbound` → `assign` → outbound-task path end-to-end (the existing test `test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign_with_matching_source_integration` constructs the source via `AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration)` where `integration` is the Integration model, which does match — but there is no test covering the deassign path or the inbound→outbound round trip through the actual task).

findings.title: `should_sync` cycle check only covers assignee sync; `sync_status_outbound` accepts `assignment_source` but the guard is not applied there
findings.body: `sync_status_outbound` was given an `assignment_source: AssignmentSource | None = None` parameter, but unlike `should_sync` (which now rejects a matching source), nothing in the shown code checks `assignment_source` inside `sync_status_outbound`, and no caller in this diff passes it. The PR description says the goal is to break "issue sync cycles" generally, but the status-sync path (which has the identical inbound-webhook → outbound-update loop shape via `sync_status_inbound`/`sync_status_outbound`) is left unprotected. Either the parameter is dead weight (and should be removed), or the status outbound path needs the same source check — as written, a Jira status change webhook can still trigger a Sentry status update that propagates back out to Jira.

findings.title: No test covers the `assignment_source_dict` parameter of the `sync_assignee_outbound` task itself
findings.body: The task gained an `assignment_source_dict` parameter and the `should_sync(..., parsed_assignment_source)` gate, but the only new tests mock `ExampleIntegration.sync_assignee_outbound` at the model layer (`tests/sentry/models/test_groupassignee.py`) and assert on the mock's call args. There is no test that runs the actual `sync_assignee_outbound` Celery task with a non-None `assignment_source_dict` and asserts that `installation.sync_assignee_outbound` is NOT invoked when the source integration matches the external issue's integration (and IS invoked when it differs). The core behavioral guarantee of this PR — the task-level skip — is therefore untested; a regression that drops the `parsed_assignment_source` argument at line 56 would pass the whole suite.

findings.title: `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` embeds a `datetime` in Celery task kwargs without serialization handling
findings.body: `sync_group_assignee_outbound` passes `assignment_source.to_dict()` (which via `asdict` includes `queued` as a `datetime` object) directly into `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(kwargs=...)`. Depending on the Celery serializer configured for the `integrations` queue, a raw `datetime` may fail to serialize (raising at enqueue time, losing the outbound sync entirely) or be serialized to a string that `AssignmentSource.from_dict` then stores as a `str` (see the related finding on `from_dict`). The code should serialize `queued` explicitly (e.g., `queued.isoformat()` in `to_dict`, with `from_dict` parsing it back) so the round trip is well-defined regardless of serializer.

findings.title: Typo in test name: `test_from_dict_inalid_data`
findings.body: The test method is named `test_from_dict_inalid_data` — a typo for `invalid`. It tests that `from_dict({"foo": "bar"})` returns `None`, which is correct behavior, but the misspelled name will show up as-is in test reports and makes the intent less discoverable. Rename to `test_from_dict_invalid_data`.
